title: Choi-Jamiołkowski isomorphism(s) and channel/state duality, naturally!
abstract: Provided a maximally entangled state vector in ${\mathcal{H}}\otimes{\mathcal{H}}$, the Choi-Jamiolkowski isomorphism of quantum information theory (or channel/state duality) produces a mapping of ${\mathsf CP}({\mathcal{H}},{\mathcal{K}})$ (completely positive maps of density operators on ${\mathcal{H}}$ tothose on ${\mathcal{K}}$) onto the density operators on ${\mathcal{K}}\otimes{\mathcal{H}}$, which extends to a unitary map. Here, ${\mathcal{H}}$ and ${\mathcal{K}}$ are {finite-dimensional} Hilbert spaces.The nature of this construction, the form of the associated formulas, and the possibility of versions which do not require an entangled vector seed, are illuminated from the perspective of {naturality}, in the sense of Eilenberg and MacLane.There is a unique such correspondence (``Choi map'') natural in both ${\mathcal{H}}$ and ${\mathcal{K}}$ which produces density operators on either ${\mathsf L}({\mathcal{H}},{\mathcal{K}})$ (Hilbert-Schmidt inner product) or ${\mathcal{K}}\otimes{\mathcal{H}}^*$ instead of ${\mathcal{K}}\otimes{\mathcal{H}}$. In particular, no entangled state input is required. There are no such binatural maps carried on ${\mathcal{K}}\otimes{\mathcal{H}}$, but those natural in only ${\mathcal{K}}$ are canonically associated with unitary maps ${\mathcal{H}}\rightarrow{\mathcal{H}}^*$ and derive from the binatural maps. The construction recovers the standard Choi-Jamiolkowski formulae and shows how they express naturality.
summary: This theoretical paper re-examines the Choi-Jamiolkowski isomorphism by employing the rigorous tools of category theory. It derives unique, natural formulations for the channel/state duality that are independent of an initial entangled state. This work refines our understanding of quantum information theory by showing that structural naturality imposes strict constraints on these fundamental isomorphisms.
main_problem: To establish a natural, invariant formulation for the Choi-Jamiolkowski isomorphism (channel/state duality) that avoids dependence on an arbitrary maximally entangled state input.
main_result: The paper identifies unique natural Choi maps, $C$ and $J$, whose existence is dictated by structural requirements of naturality in category theory, showing that the conventional CJ isomorphism is a specific instance of this general structure.
method: The analysis heavily relies on category theory concepts, specifically naturality, functors, and the rigorous definition of dual spaces and tensor products for linear operators on Hilbert spaces.
model_or_system: The theory concerns Completely Positive (CP) maps ($\Lambda$) acting on density operators defined on finite-dimensional Hilbert spaces ($\mathcal{H}$ and $\mathcal{K}$), which form the core of quantum information theory.
key_observables: The Choi map itself, $\mathcal{C}(\Lambda)$, and its associated trace ($	ext{Tr} \circ \mathcal{C}$), which characterizes the relationship between channels and states.
important_parameters: The dimensions of the Hilbert spaces ($\dim \mathcal{H}, \dim \mathcal{K}$), and the structure of the underlying unitary maps.
main_assumptions: The primary assumption is that the structure of the isomorphism must be natural in both input and output spaces ($\mathcal{H}$ and $\mathcal{K}$), leading to the rejection of the standard state-dependent formulation.
paper_structure: The paper systematically builds mathematical machinery by defining dual spaces and the natural isomorphism $T: L(H, K) 	o K \otimes H^*$. It then applies functorial arguments to derive and compare the unique natural Choi maps ($\mathcal{J}$ and $\mathcal{C}$) against the conventional CJ isomorphism.
why_interesting: It provides a deep, abstract mathematical underpinning for a cornerstone result in quantum information theory, suggesting that the physical constraints (naturality) dictate the mathematical form of the duality.
